boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten documented Grinnell spaces for focused work, collaboration, creative projects, student activities, and low-key time together.

cards.title: Settle In Among the Plants
cards.subtitle: A top-floor study lounge in Steiner Hall
cards.notes: Head to Steiner Hall’s top floor for soft lighting, comfortable seating, school supplies, and a setting designed for focused work or body doubling.
cards.short_summary: A plant-filled academic-semester workspace open to the entire student community.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell says the Partners’ Study Lounge is open to all students and offers plants, comfortable seating, school supplies, snacks, and space for body doubling.
cards.source_title: A Cozy Corner for Concentration: Discover the Partners’ Study Lounge at Steiner Hall
cards.access_notes: Located on Steiner Hall’s top floor; the cited page lists daily academic-semester access from 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.

cards.title: Build Something Beyond the Classroom
cards.subtitle: A College-community makerspace at 927 Broad Street
cards.notes: Stop in during open hours to explore fabrication tools, then take the required training before attempting 3D printing, sewing, woodworking, or metalwork.
cards.short_summary: A downtown workshop where students can learn tools, make crafts, and prototype projects.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell identifies the Stew Makerspace at 927 Broad Street as a College-community space offering tools, training, and workshops in design and fabrication.
cards.access_notes: Student access is tied to posted open hours, training requirements, and tool-specific procedures; confirm availability before visiting.

cards.title: Take a Reflective Break by the Garden
cards.subtitle: A shared teaching garden east of Pine Tree House
cards.notes: Walk east of Pine Tree House to see the teaching garden, or connect with its program before planning hands-on gardening or group learning there.
cards.short_summary: A campus garden combining food production with reflection, creativity, and shared learning.
cards.evidence_claim: The College describes its garden east of Pine Tree House as a shared teaching and learning space for creativity, reflection, cultural enrichment, and food production.
cards.access_notes: Outdoor viewing may vary with weather and seasonal operations; participation in garden work should be coordinated with the program.

cards.title: Check the Student-Activity Calendar
cards.subtitle: A film, performance, recreation, and gathering venue
cards.notes: Look for a scheduled film, concert, wellness program, or student event; the building also contains an informal lounge and the GORP office.
cards.short_summary: A flexible student-activities hub with a cinema, concert hall, courtyard, and lounge.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell says the Harris Center houses weekend student activities and includes a cinema, concert hall, informal lounge, courtyard, and GORP office.
cards.access_notes: Event spaces may be scheduled or restricted; consult the current College event listing before planning a visit.

cards.title: Meet Where Four Pavilions Connect
cards.subtitle: The three-story center of the Humanities and Social Studies Center
cards.notes: Use the central atrium as a rendezvous point, then branch into the HSSC’s academic commons, research rooms, or team rooms when available.
cards.short_summary: A daylight-filled connector surrounded by spaces built for study, meetings, and collaboration.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell states that the HSSC’s four pavilions connect through a central three-story atrium and that students use the building’s commons, research rooms, and team rooms.
cards.source_title: Grinnell College Celebrates Humanities and Social Studies Center with Dedication Event
cards.access_notes: Use depends on normal HSSC building access; classrooms, research rooms, and team rooms may be scheduled.

cards.title: Bring a Group to the South Pavilion
cards.subtitle: A named collaboration commons inside the HSSC
cards.notes: Choose this South Pavilion commons when a project needs room for several people to gather, compare notes, and work together outside class.
cards.short_summary: A named HSSC commons specifically documented as a place for students to gather and study together.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell’s alumni site identifies Gordon Smith Commons in the HSSC South Pavilion and says it provides ample room for students to gather and study together.
cards.source_title: Trio of 1972 alumnae explain inspirations to name spaces in HSSC
cards.access_notes: Located in the HSSC South Pavilion; access follows current HSSC building rules and any posted space reservations.

cards.title: Use the Campus Living Room
cards.subtitle: Dining, mail, meetings, recreation, and lounges in one building
cards.notes: Meet here when a group needs flexible options: lounges, recreational areas, meeting rooms, the gallery, mailroom, and dining are all under one roof.
cards.short_summary: A central campus gathering building that combines daily errands with social and meeting space.
cards.evidence_claim: The College calls the Joe Rosenfield ’25 Center its central gathering place and lists lounges, recreational areas, meeting rooms, classrooms, a gallery, dining, and mail services.
cards.access_notes: Individual rooms, offices, dining areas, and services may follow separate schedules or eligibility rules.

cards.title: Meet Beneath the Global Flags
cards.subtitle: A casual gathering spot inside the Rosenfield Center
cards.notes: Use the seating as a clear meetup point between commitments; bring an accepted payment method only if you plan to order food or coffee.
cards.short_summary: A photographed campus café setting where students can sit together over coffee, lunch, or snacks.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell presents Spencer Grill as a place to meet friends for coffee, lunch, baked goods, or a snack and notes accepted campus payment methods.
cards.access_notes: Food and drinks require purchase; consult the current hours link on the official page before going.

cards.title: Turn an Assignment Into Media
cards.subtitle: Editing, scanning, recording, and equipment checkout in Burling’s lower level
cards.notes: Bring a digital project to the lower level for Mac editing stations and scanning; ask the circulation desk about cameras, recorders, or other checkout gear.
cards.short_summary: A first-come digital workspace equipped for video, audio, scanning, and media production.
cards.evidence_claim: A current College library article says the lower-level Burling Digital Studio has seven Mac editing workstations, scanning equipment, and technology available through circulation.
cards.access_notes: The cited article says workstation use is first-come, first-served; equipment checkout and specialized tools have separate procedures.

cards.title: Practice the Presentation Before Class
cards.subtitle: Quiet study and group rooms on Noyce’s second floor
cards.notes: Take a group to one of Kistle’s four first-come study rooms; choose the projector-equipped room when you need to rehearse slides together.
cards.short_summary: A science-library study setting with carrels, tables, and four rooms for collaborative work.
cards.evidence_claim: Grinnell’s 2026 study-space guide says Kistle Science Library has quiet study areas and four first-come group rooms, including one with a projector.
cards.access_notes: Located on the second floor of Noyce Science Center; group rooms are first-come, first-served under the cited guidance.
